# Connect your agent

Grain speaks the Model Context Protocol, so agent clients such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf and Codex can run queries, list schemas, and describe tables against your own databases.

## Connect with one command

After installing Grain, run:

```
grain connect
```

Grain lists the agents it supports, marks the ones it found, and connects only the ones you pick. To connect without prompts, name them: `grain connect --agent claude-desktop --agent cursor`. `grain disconnect` removes Grain from your agents.

## Connect manually

[Install Grain](https://grain.tools/docs/install) first. Every client then runs the same command, on macOS, Linux, and Windows:

```
grain --stdio
```

That is the whole setup contract. Everything below is how to hand that one command to a particular client. `--stdio` takes no value.

The bridge attaches to the shared Grain service when it is available. If the service cannot be reached, it reports isolated mode; queries still work, but their sessions do not appear in the editor.

Claude Code, Codex, VS Code, Cursor and Windsurf pick up the PATH the installer set, so `grain` is enough. Claude Desktop does not read your shell’s PATH, so it gets the full path; see its section.

## Before you connect

1. **Have connections.** Install the [extension](https://grain.tools/docs/install) and add a connection profile, or supply profiles through `GRAIN_CONNECTIONS`, as described in Headless connections.
2. **Check that MCP is on.** MCP is on by default. If you turned it off, turn `grain.mcpEnabled` back on in the Grain settings panel, or set `"mcp": { "enabled": true }` in `~/.grain/daemon.json`. While MCP is off, the bridge refuses with a message instead of failing quietly.
3. **Leave [safe mode](https://grain.tools/docs/safe-mode) on** unless you intend agents to run mutating SQL.

## Clients that take a command

### Claude Code

```
claude mcp add grain -- grain --stdio
```

### Cursor

Settings → **MCP Servers** → **Add new MCP server**. Type `command`, name `grain`, command `grain --stdio`.

### Windsurf

Settings → **Cascade** → **MCP Servers** → **Add Server**, then paste the same JSON as Claude Desktop below into `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json`.

### VS Code and Copilot

VS Code reads MCP servers from `.vscode/mcp.json` in the workspace, or from your user `mcp.json` via **MCP: Open User Configuration** in the command palette. Note the key is `servers`, not `mcpServers`:

```
{
  "servers": {
    "grain": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "grain",
      "args": ["--stdio"]
    }
  }
}
```

Copilot Chat in agent mode picks the server up from the same file.

### Codex

Add the server to `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```
[mcp_servers.grain]
command = "grain"
args = ["--stdio"]
```

## Clients that take only a config file

Claude Desktop has no command-line registration, so it is configured by file. It starts servers without your shell’s PATH, so the command is the full path to `grain`: `/Users/you/.grain/bin/grain` on macOS (run `echo "$HOME/.grain/bin/grain"` to print yours), `C:\Users\you\.grain\bin\grain.cmd` on Windows (double each backslash inside JSON).

Config file location:

- **macOS**: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`
- **Windows**: `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json`. Paste that path into `Win + R`; create the file if it is not there.

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "grain": {
      "command": "/Users/you/.grain/bin/grain",
      "args": ["--stdio"]
    }
  }
}
```

Restart the client fully after editing. If the file already has an `mcpServers` object, add only the `"grain"` entry inside it.

## Headless connections

By default the bridge attaches to the daemon your editor is already running, so agent queries land in the same result tabs as your own. `GRAIN_EMBEDDED=1` forces an isolated daemon rather than attaching to a shared one, which is useful in CI. Save connection profiles through Grain and enter credentials through its one-time credential page.

### Environment variables

| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `GRAIN_CONNECTIONS` | JSON array of connection profiles, for headless use |
| `GRAIN_MCP_SAFE_MODE` | `false` allows mutating SQL. Defaults to `true` |
| `GRAIN_MAX_ROWS` | Row cap for query tools. Defaults to `10000` |
| `GRAIN_HOME` | Which config directory is used, and so which daemon |
| `GRAIN_EMBEDDED` | `1` forces an isolated daemon instead of attaching |

## Without installing

A machine that has Node.js 20 or newer can run Grain from npm instead, with no install step:

```
npx -y grain-tools --stdio
```

`-y` skips npm’s install prompt, which a client could never answer. Use this for evaluation and headless automation. It needs Node on every machine and can run in isolated mode when no shared service is available, so installed `grain` is the recommended desktop path.

## Advanced HTTP connection

Direct HTTP is a separately gated rollout surface. Use it only when Grain settings explicitly offers a ready-made HTTP client configuration. It requires a bearer token and exposes a port and credential to the client, so stdio remains the normal setup.

## The tools you get

Grain advertises 20 tools. A tool a profile does not permit is still advertised and still answers, with an explicit refusal naming the profile, so an agent can tell “not allowed here” from “does not exist”.

| Group | Tools |
|---|---|
| Query | `run_query`, `cancel_query` |
| Schema | `list_schemas`, `list_tables`, `describe_table` |
| Connections | `list_connectors`, `list_connections`, `test_connection`, `create_connection_draft`, `save_connection`, `delete_connection`, `request_connection_credentials` |
| Result tabs | `get_tab_info`, `close_tab`, `list_sessions` |
| Demo | `get_demo_dataset` |
| Other tools | `render_chart`, `save_chart`, `list_charts` |
| Telemetry | `record_ui_event` |

An agent attached through the packaged bridge runs under the **agent** profile: it may read, query, draft connections, and request the one-time password page. Only `save_connection` and `delete_connection` are refused.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
|---|---|
| No tools appear in the client | The client was not fully restarted, or cannot find `grain`. Use the full path for Claude Desktop |
| `grain` not found in a terminal | Open a new terminal after installing, or add `~/.grain/bin` to your PATH if you installed with `GRAIN_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1` |
| The bridge starts and then stops | `grain.mcpEnabled` is off. Turn it on, or set `mcp.enabled` in `~/.grain/daemon.json` |
| Agent queries are not in the grid | The bridge found no shared daemon and started its own. The `initialize` response reports `Grain isolation mode: shared` or `isolated` |
| A tool answers with a refusal | The profile refuses that tool’s resource class. The message names both |

## Identifiers

VS Code extension id`pattrnlabs.grain`

npm package name`grain-tools`

stdio command`grain --stdio`

stdio command without installing (needs Node)`npx -y grain-tools --stdio`

## MCP Configuration

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "grain": {
      "command": "grain",
      "args": [
        "--stdio"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```
